title: unified-rollouts: enhance canary/A-B/shadow autorollback workflows
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: stabilize and standardize rollout workflows across canary, A/B, and shadow modes by improving probing, multi-metric matching, and automated rollback policies. This PR implements: 1) staged probing for shadow traffic to detect silent regressions before shifting weight; 2) consolidated A/B experiment primitives that share metric windows and evaluation hooks with canaries; 3) multi-metric autorollback engine with configurable matching rules (threshold, direction, weighted scoring); 4) safety guards to prevent cascading rollbacks across related routes; 5) observability hooks (per-rollout metric tags and tracing spans) so SRE and product can quickly diagnose regressions. Description of change: - rollout controller: add staged probe controller for shadow traffic and probing schedule config; unify evaluation pipeline so canary and A/B use same aggregator; add composite-metric evaluator with support for JSON-defined metric expressions; implement autorollback decision service with tunable hysteresis and backoff; integrate per-rollout tracing and tags. - API: extend RolloutSpec to include probeSchedule, compositeMetric, and rollbackPolicy sections; update REST + SDK validation to accept new fields. - E2E/testing: add synthetic workload generator and deterministic simulator to exercise staged shadow probing and rollback paths. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-3421) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] automated e2e simulation - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] performance benchmark run (latency/regression check) How this was tested: local unit tests, CI integration, deterministic e2e rollout simulator, manual smoke on staging with a short canary on a non-critical route. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag; gradually enable on internal staging environments for 48h, then enable on low-traffic customer routes for 72h with monitoring and manual cutoff; full enable after 1 week if no regressions. Related: ENG-3421, ENG-3987, SUP-77. Notes: prioritizes safety; default policies conservative.
